ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, general partners, limited partners, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada designations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, Criminal Code listed terrorist entities, and PEP/vulnerable-position indicators. Given the Low_Risk_Standard banking tier of the executive headhunting business, standard customer due diligence applies, with enhanced due diligence triggered by non-Canadian PEP status, irregular source of funds, or any sanction-list hit; retainer payments via wire or Wise B2B are subject to ongoing transaction monitoring consistent with the PCMLTFA enterprise-wide risk assessment framework.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) operated by Service Alberta - albertacorporateregistry.ca; NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) national search report mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The limited partnership name may be in English or French. Names in English must end with 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'LP' or 'L.P.'; the French 'société en commandite' is accepted. Latin script and Arabic numerals are required for filing; any transliterated non-Latin name must be accompanied by a certified translation. A NUANS search report is mandatory and must be submitted with the registration filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Corporate Registry refuses a proposed name, obtain the written statement of reasons from the Director of Partnerships (Service Alberta). Submit a written reconsideration brief addressing confusing similarity, supported by the NUANS report and any registered trademark evidence, with the applicable CAD 40 reconsideration fee. If the Director affirms the refusal, file an originating application for judicial review before the Alberta Court of King's Bench within 30 days of the reconsideration decision. Alternative names may be reserved without prejudice while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the registered office only if a physical street address in Alberta is maintained for service of process and access to statutory records. A pure virtual mailbox without a fixed Alberta street address is not compliant. For the Employment Agency Business Licence, a fixed physical place of business in Alberta (including a declared home office) is mandatory and cannot be satisfied solely by a virtual office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~5-10% annual probability) for the registered office during the pre-licensing stage; moderate (~15-25% annual probability) for the employment agency premises once the licence is active, given inspection powers of Employment Standards officers under the Employment Standards Code.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 51-78; Fair Trading Act, RSA 2000, c F-2, and Employment Agency Business Licensing Regulation, Alta Reg 190/1999
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (filings accepted through authorized Registry Agents and the corporate registry online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration of Limited Partnership form (Alberta Corporate Registry LP-01 / online Limited Partnership Registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta limited partnership. Limited partners may contribute cash, property, or services as agreed in the partnership agreement; no escrow or statutory deposit account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: the Board ratifies the formation of the Alberta limited partnership (the 'LP') and approves the execution and filing of all registration instruments with the Alberta Corporate Registry, including the Registration of Limited Partnership and any required statements. RESOLVED: the Partnership Agreement presented to this Board is approved and adopted as the binding governance instrument of the LP. RESOLVED: ABC Corporate Services Inc. is appointed initial general partner and Jane Doe is appointed authorized representative to execute statutory filings, open banking facilities, and direct formation counsel. RESOLVED: the officers of the corporate general partner are authorized to pay all filing fees and take all lawful actions necessary to activate the LP's operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Alberta LP Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - NUANS search via authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a coordinated NUANS name search to confirm the proposed LP name is distinguishable from existing Alberta business names, corporate names, and registered trade-marks. Submit a Name Reservation Request through a registry agent or the online portal and obtain a name reservation number valid for 90 days. For bilingual operations, reserve English and French variants simultaneously.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name (English and/or French variants)
Signed name reservation authorization letter
Government-issued identification of the applicant / authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as non-distinguishable, select and reserve a new name; the rejected reservation may be amended without loss of priority only if no intervening third-party registration occurs. A fresh reservation application and fee are otherwise required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and notarization (internal governance step, not filed with the registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the limited partnership agreement covering capital contributions, profit sharing, management rights of the general partner, restrictions on limited partner participation (Partnership Act s. 56), withdrawal and transfer provisions, and dispute resolution. Complete the statutory particulars (name, registered office, general partner name and address, contribution schedule) to be transcribed into the LP registration form.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement
Schedule of capital contributions by each limited partner
Consent of each limited partner to the agreement terms
Registered office consent letter from the office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry review identifies defective particulars, amend the partnership agreement by unanimous partner consent or revise the registered office consent letter, then re-file the corrected registration form. No court filing is required for ministerial corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Registration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - online Corporate Registry system or in-person at any authorized Registry Agent office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Registration of Limited Partnership form (LP-01) electronically or in person, quoting the name reservation number, the Alberta registered office address, the full legal name and address of each general partner, the corporate general partner's director information (if applicable), and the names or particulars of all limited partners. Pay the prescribed CAD 50 filing fee. The LP comes into existence upon the registry's issuance of the registration confirmation.
required_dossiers: Completed Registration of Limited Partnership form (LP-01)
Name reservation number
Registered office address within Alberta
Identification of general partner (and directors, if the general partner is a corporation)
Filing fee payment in accepted form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Request for Additional Information or deficiency notice from the registry within 30 calendar days; correct the stated rejection reason (e.g., incomplete general partner details, invalid registered office address) and re-submit. Expedited filing is available for urgent transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number Enrolment and Municipal Business Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and the local municipal licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence & Revenue or City of Edmonton Business Licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the LP registration confirmation and partnership agreement, register the LP with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a 9-digit Business Number for the partnership. Activate GST/HST and payroll accounts where the LP has employees or taxable revenue above the applicable registration threshold. Apply to the municipal licensing authority for a general business licence for an office-based executive search agency.
required_dossiers: Alberta LP registration confirmation / certificate
General partner resolution appointing the authorized representative for CRA and licensing
Identification of each partner (date of birth for individuals, incorporation number for corporate partners)
Municipal business licence application form and fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For CRA issues, correct account activation through My Business Account or by calling the CRA Business Enquiries line. For municipal licence refusals, address zoning, signage, or use-compliance objections and submit a revised application or minor variance request to the municipal planning department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta - Consumer and Regulatory Services (Fair Trading Act licensing); Alberta Occupational Health and Safety; local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the LP's executive search and headhunting services constitute an 'employment agency' under the Employment Agency Business Licensing Regulation (Alta Reg 190/1999). If the agency charges job-seekers or performs general placement services, obtain an Employment Agency Licence; a retainer-only executive search paid exclusively by employers may fall within the employer-pays exemption and require only a municipal business licence. In addition, complete a workplace hazard assessment, adopt an OHS policy, and obtain a fire safety inspection clearance for the registered office premises.
required_dossiers: Employment Agency Licence application (if applicable under Alta Reg 190/1999)
Copy of LP registration confirmation and municipal business licence
Workplace hazard assessment and OHS harassment/violence prevention policy
Municipal fire safety inspection certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Employment Agency Licence is refused, revise the fee model to an employer-paid retainer structure and resubmit with supporting client contracts. For fire safety or OHS deficiencies, implement corrective measures identified in the inspection report and request a re-inspection before commencing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Service Alberta - Consumer and Regulatory Services (Employment Agency Licensing) and the applicable municipal business licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence & Revenue or City of Edmonton Business Licensing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (general office operations) and Employment Agency Licence under the Employment Agency Business Licensing Regulation, Alta Reg 190/1999, where the placement activity falls within the Fair Trading Act definition

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based executive search and headhunting services; no prescribed activity listed under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 or the Activities Designation Regulation, Alta Reg 276/2003
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams generated. The LP must comply with municipal solid-waste and recycling bylaws, commercial stormwater discharge rules, and any landlord-imposed waste-handling protocols applicable to the leased office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certification confirming compliance with the Alberta Fire Code and local fire bylaw; building occupancy permit verifying structural load, egress, and accessibility under the Safety Codes Act; and an Occupational Health and Safety clearance confirming compliance with the OHS Code, including the workplace harassment and violence prevention plan and first-aid requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority responsible for currency issuance and monetary policy. Canada operates a free-floating exchange-rate system, and there is no separate foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control bureau. The Minister of Finance and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervise banks and payment-service providers, but no central-bank approval is required for cross-border funds transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. An Alberta limited partnership may freely receive offshore retainers, invoice foreign clients in CAD or foreign currencies, and remit profits to non-resident partners without exchange-control authorisation. The principal profit-remittance hurdles are fiscal, not monetary: the LP must file all required Canadian income-tax returns, allocate Canadian-source partnership income correctly to non-resident partners, and address any applicable withholding obligations under the Income Tax Act for payments of interest, royalties, or management-type fees. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) may require an information return for distributions to non-resident partners, but there is no exchange-convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no statutory conversion ratio for inward commercial receipts. Executive-search service fees received from abroad may be held in CAD, USD, or another convertible currency in a Canadian or foreign bank account. All transactions remain subject only to general anti-money-laundering reporting, including FINTRAC large-transaction reporting for cash or mixed-cash deposits of CAD 10,000 or more and to the requirement that wire transfers carry complete originator and beneficiary information.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — CAD/USD business chequing; Capital Escrow / capital-contribution clearing sub-ledger can be attached
Operational Account — Canadian-dollar business chequing with USD cross-border payment capability
Operational Account — Business banking bundle with USD clearing and international wire capability
Operational Account — Canadian business chequing with BMO Harris cross-border USD integration
Operational Account — Standard business operating account; straightforward onboarding for low-risk service entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an auxiliary payment rail, but Low as a primary treasury or deposit account. Offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) are not authorised banks in Canada under the Bank Act, cannot accept deposits in CDIC-insured accounts, and cannot issue Canadian IBANs. They may only provide e-money settlement through a Canadian-registered money services business (MSB) or by partnering with a regulated Canadian financial institution. Wise B2B is operationally viable for low-value and mid-value cross-border retainer wires, contractor disbursements, and small vendor payments; however, the primary liquidity pool must be maintained with a Schedule I Canadian bank to reduce MSB counterparty risk, FINTRAC registration complexity, and potential frozen-funds events. For large executive-search fees, a direct SWIFT wire from the client to the LP's Schedule I bank account remains the cleanest rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Canadian-resident general partner or authorised signatory, remote onboarding with live video verification is accepted by all major Schedule I banks. For non-resident partners or foreign corporate general partners, banks generally mandate an in-person branch meeting or a notarised identity verification completed at a Canadian consulate, accompanied by passport, proof of address, and source-of-wealth documentation. A fully remote opening is possible where the LP has a Canadian registered office, an Alberta-registered agent for service, and a Canadian-resident authorised signatory; even then, enhanced due diligence will require notarised identity certificates for every individual beneficial owner holding 25 percent or more of the partnership or controlling the corporate general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque limited-partnership ownership structure, including nominee limited partners, bearer-like interests, or trust-arranged beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Alberta limited-partnership agreement; current registration extract from the Alberta Corporate/Partnership Registry; register of limited partners; beneficial-ownership register identifying all natural persons owning 25 percent or more; declarations confirming no nominee ownership; bank reference letters for each significant partner; explanation of the commercial purpose of the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners resident in FATF low- or uncooperative-jurisdictions, or absence of a Canadian resident signatory on the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passports and proof of residential address for all non-resident partners; independent corporate-registry search from the partner's home jurisdiction; source-of-wealth letter; source-of-funds evidence for capital contributions; clearing explanation of the executive-search business model; commitment to maintain a Canadian-resident authorised signatory and to provide annual partnership financial statements to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound retainer wires from foreign clients whose jurisdiction or corporate registration does not align with the stated target-search markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed C-suite retainer agreement or master services agreement; detailed headhunting scope and search mandate; itemised invoices referencing ISIC 7830 / NAICS 561312 services; corporate register excerpts for the client; correspondence and search-project evidence (e.g., candidate pipeline, interview notes, placement contracts) demonstrating the genuine commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent disbursements via Wise B2B or other non-bank payment-service providers to overseas independent search associates or contractors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC MSB registration certificate of the payment-service provider where applicable; signed independent-contractor or partnership-remittance agreements with overseas associates; service invoices from each receiving consultant; a regular disbursement register linking each transfer to a specific search mandate; annual reconciliation of all PSP accounts with the LP's general ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital contribution routing requires a SWIFT MT103 or domestic wire from the partner's own bank account to the LP's Schedule I bank account, with the wire reference clearly identifying the partner, the LP name, and the phrase 'LP Capital Contribution'. No foreign-exchange approval is needed, but the bank may request the partnership agreement and a capital-account statement to distinguish partner contributions from taxable revenue. For wires exceeding CAD 10,000, the bank must capture complete originator information for FINTRAC reporting; statutory purpose is generally recorded as 'other business services' or 'capital contribution'. Investment Canada Act notification is not triggered by ordinary capital contributions to an executive-search LP unless an acquisition of Canadian control is involved, which is not applicable for this headhunting scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for retainer wires is direct SWIFT MT103 from the LP's CAD/USD bank account to the beneficiary's bank account, with full beneficiary identification and a purpose code referring to 'management consulting / executive search services'. For high-value settlements, commercial letters of credit are not a natural fit for executive-search services because there are no shipped goods or transport documents; if a client insists on a trade instrument, an at-sight commercial LC through a Canadian Schedule I bank can be structured around invoice-and-receipt presentation, but SWIFT MT103 remains the industry-standard and lowest-cost rail. Wise B2B is approved as a secondary rail for small and medium payments, contractor disbursements, and urgent cross-border payments, provided every payment is supported by an invoice, engagement letter, and clear commercial rationale.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, GBP/CAD) executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank treasury desk for commercial retainer-flow hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-emerging-market currencies where physical delivery is not possible, only where the underlying exposure is a verified cross-border search fee
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps / currency swaps) for larger capital rationing and balance-sheet hedging under an ISDA/CSA master agreement with a qualified Canadian bank

Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options and zero-cost collars used for retainer-billing margin protection, provided they are transacted through a licensed bank dealer and subject to the LP's declared hedging policy
